diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's own fibre path has a marginal and unstable optical RX level. RX varies between normal and degraded levels, currently measuring -26.88 dBm, while TX power, TX bias, and distance remain stable. This indicates fibre-path loss or an intermittent connector/splice issue rather than laser, ONU, PON, OLT, router, or authentication failure.
evidence: The live ONU responds and is online, so this is not an ONU-offline fault.
The live RX level is -26.88 dBm, which is in the degraded range and explains intermittent service quality.
The seven-day RX telemetry has wide real variation, approximately from -22.0 to -27.0 dBm, exceeding the healthy +/-0.3 dBm noise floor.
The telemetry starts just inside the degraded band at -25.07 dBm, so this is a marginal fibre path oscillating in and out of usable range rather than a qualifying normal-to-degraded decline.
TX power remains near 2.3 dBm, TX bias remains healthy and flat around 11 mA, and distance remains constant at 203, ruling out laser degradation and distance/path-record change.
Peers on EPON0/6 are online with healthy optical readings, so the fault is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON port or splitter.
The OLT answers ping, SNMP, and subtree queries; OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal.
The router heartbeat is healthy, and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1036 rather than factory-default VLAN 46.

RADIUS exists, matches the CRM line ID, and has no inconsistencies. Seven sessions in 24 hours is elevated but below the 8-session flapping threshold, so session behavior is a symptom of the marginal optical path, not an authentication fault.
The stored -22.41 dBm reading is 141 minutes old and is superseded by the live degraded reading.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service to inspect, clean, and reseat the ONU and fibre connectors, then test the customer drop and splice path with an optical power meter and OTDR. Repair or replace the damaged connector, splice, or drop fibre as required. Recheck RX stability after repair and monitor the line for at least 24 hours.

ground_truth.root_cause: Intermittent attenuation in the customer's fibre path, most consistent with a marginal connector or a bend that moves with temperature; the link crosses in and out of usable signal.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -22.41 dBm is inside the normal band and on its own looks fine
The cached reading is 141 minutes old, so it may not represent current state
Live RX of -26.88 dBm is 4.5 dB worse than cached, a gap far outside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between roughly -22 and -27 dBm on a sub-daily cycle
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU is healthy
Peers on EPON0/6 read normal, so the PON port and splitter are not involved
Seven sessions in 24h is elevated above the 2-3 baseline and tracks the signal excursions
An oscillating marginal link points to a physical fault that moves, not a fixed loss
distractors: The cached RX reading is inside the normal band and invites a no_fault conclusion
Seven sessions is elevated but sits inside the 2.9% of customers who do 4-7 normally
Erratic traffic could be read as ordinary usage variation
